recent_posts.title: Kotlin Ecosystem Mentorship Program: Results and Winners
recent_posts.summary: The Kotlin Foundation's pilot Ecosystem Mentorship Program has concluded, with four pairs successfully completing the two-month initiative. Mentor Ruslan and mentee Clare Kinery won the grand prize — a trip to KotlinConf 2026 in Munich — after Clare contributed UI/UX improvements to the BitChat Android project. Three other pairs also completed the program, contributing to projects like Calf, FlowMVI, and Heron. The program received 80 mentee and 29 mentor applications, and the Foundation plans to continue it. Key lessons include the importance of clear task scoping, explicit async communication expectations, and the mutual value mentorship creates for both contributors and maintainers.

recent_posts.title: The MPS 2026.1 Early Access Program Has Started
recent_posts.summary: JetBrains has launched the MPS 2026.1 Early Access Program. Key changes include migration to IntelliJ Platform 2026.1, JDK 25, and Kotlin 2.3 with restored KLib-based Kotlin stubs support. New features include natural language-aware name policy checking via Grazie integration, multi-line splitting of binary operations in the editor, a new read-only-inspector boolean editor style, transitive dependency support in Build Language, more reliable migrations using recorded module descriptor dependencies, several long-standing Java stubs bug fixes, a modernized MPSProject lifecycle mechanism, and Wayland as the default display protocol on supported Linux systems.

recent_posts.title: Make Your Plugin Remote Development-Ready
recent_posts.summary: JetBrains has introduced guidance for building split-mode-aware plugins for JetBrains IDEs. In split mode, the IDE runs a frontend client and a backend process separately — potentially on different machines, in Docker, or in the cloud. Plugin developers must now consider where each part of their plugin runs, separating UI/latency-sensitive code to the frontend and backend logic accordingly. The recommended architecture works in both split and monolithic IDE modes, so no duplicate implementations are needed. Resources include a video overview, a modular plugin template on GitHub, official documentation with a step-by-step splitting guide, and a community forum.

recent_posts.title: Python Unplugged on PyTV: Key Takeaways From Our Community Conference
recent_posts.summary: Key takeaways from Python Unplugged on PyTV, JetBrains' first fully online Python community conference held March 4, 2026 in Amsterdam. Over 5,500 attended live with 110,000 watching on demand. Nine highlights are covered: Python's depth beyond beginner use, the role of community (PyLadies, PSF), AI's dual impact on open source maintainership, agentic coding workflows, open-source AI ecosystems (Hugging Face), LlamaIndex for document-centric agents, Polars' high-performance data processing with query profiling, incremental typing in Python, and Django's ongoing relevance despite outdated perceptions.

recent_posts.title: How to Make Code Highlighting-Friendly
recent_posts.summary: Introduces the concept of 'highlighting complexity' — how code structure affects IDE analysis speed and resource usage — and provides actionable Scala coding practices to reduce it. Recommendations include separating code into modules, putting classes in separate files, defining classes in packages rather than objects, keeping classes and methods small, avoiding wildcard imports (especially for implicits), preferring imports over mixins, declaring members private where possible, specifying explicit type annotations, and favoring standard language features over macros. These practices improve IDE responsiveness, reduce CPU/memory usage, and also benefit incremental compilation. The principles apply equally to AI-generated code.

recent_posts.title: IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3.5 is Out!
recent_posts.summary: IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3.5 has been released with a targeted performance fix for Spring projects. The key change prevents Spring bean declaration searches from triggering during typing or code completion, resulting in smoother completion behavior in Spring-based projects. This patch is specifically relevant for users who have not yet upgraded to v2026.1. The update is available via the IDE itself, JetBrains Toolbox App, Ubuntu snaps, or direct download.

recent_posts.title: Developer Ecosystem Survey 2026 – Take Part in One of the Largest Developer Studies
recent_posts.summary: JetBrains is running the 10th edition of its annual Developer Ecosystem Survey, inviting developers worldwide to share their experiences with tools, technologies, and challenges in modern software development. The survey takes about 30 minutes and participants can win prizes including a MacBook Pro 16", Amazon gift cards, and JetBrains subscriptions. Results will be published as detailed infographics and reports, with anonymized raw data also made available publicly.

recent_posts.title: Stop Sending IDE-Catchable AI Code Errors to Review
recent_posts.summary: AI coding tools are increasing PR volume while introducing a distinct error profile — unused constructs, hardcoded values, and security vulnerabilities more common than in human-written code. Research shows reviewers apply less scrutiny to AI-generated code, and DORA data links rising AI adoption to a 7.2% drop in delivery stability per 25% adoption increase. Around 20–25% of AI code hallucinations are catchable via automated static analysis before a PR is raised. The post argues engineering leaders should ensure at least one IDE in every developer's workflow runs deep, whole-project structural analysis — citing JetBrains IDEs and Qodana as tools that do this — to protect reviewer capacity for the errors only humans can catch.

recent_posts.title: What is dogfooding? How JetBrains builds better developer tools
recent_posts.summary: JetBrains explains how dogfooding — using their own tools in real daily workflows — is central to their product development culture. Engineers, designers, and product managers build with IntelliJ IDEA, track work in YouTrack, and test new tools like Junie internally before any external release. Concrete examples include Rider being used internally in 2016 when it was still crash-prone, and Junie being refined through internal use months before closed beta. The practice creates tight feedback loops, fosters empathy with users, and builds team ownership. The post ends with a call to join JetBrains careers.
